title: Atonement
definition: Atonement is the saving work of Christ by which He deals with sin, satisfies God's justice, and reconciles sinners to God through His death.
summary: Atonement is the saving work of Christ by which He deals with sin, satisfies God's justice, and reconciles sinners to God through His death.
christFocus: Jesus is the atoning sacrifice who gives Himself for sinners, bearing guilt and opening the way for guilty people to be forgiven, cleansed, and brought near to God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Atonement answers the deepest problem sinners face: guilt before a holy God. Sin cannot be brushed aside, renamed, or healed by human effort. It must be dealt with before God in truth and righteousness.

Scripture shows that sacrifice, blood, priesthood, and forgiveness all point forward to Christ. He is not merely an example of love or courage; He is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.

At the cross, mercy and justice meet. Christ bears what sinners deserved so that forgiveness can be given without God denying His holiness. Atonement means salvation is not wishful thinking; it is secured by Jesus Himself.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People carrying guilt need more than encouragement. They need to know whether sin can actually be forgiven and whether God can receive them without pretending evil does not matter.

Atonement keeps the Gospel from becoming shallow. Christ did not simply suffer beside sinners; He suffered for sinners, and that is why the broken, ashamed, addicted, and guilty may come to God through Him.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to Christ as the One who made atonement for sin. Stop trying to pay for what only Jesus could bear, and let His cross lead you into repentance, worship, assurance, and grateful obedience.
